reply_text:
I've checked the self-talk candidates against futon2's code; now I'm writing up the ones that hold.㊥ (self-talk, checked) Five of the eight self-talk candidates hold up against futon2's code:
- 🈲 constrain is the grain gate refusing a candidate.
- ㊩ is R8 computing the gap between what it predicted and what it observed.
- ㊟ qualify is R3 moving a belief.
- ㊫ explore is R4 rolling a policy forward.
- 🈝 defer is the abstain act.

🈕 extend at R17 doesn't hold. The step that learns new structure there has never accumulated on a live tick, and the R17 step that does run removes structure. The morning brief is now in the file as the WM's 🈸. It sits outside the click, which is why no click act names ask-action. Both are in futon2 `89957f588`.

㊬ (what "holds up" means) For each candidate I opened the function and its call site this turn: `grain_gate.clj:65` called at `flight_runner.clj:944`; `free_energy.clj:203` tagged `:R8` at `war_machine.clj:6508`; `war_machine.clj:830` tagged `:R3` at `:6502`; `forward_model.clj:308` called at `efe.clj:644`. That shows a live function does the step the mark names. It doesn't show the step is recorded with that mark, because nothing records it that way yet. For R4, I didn't check whether live clicks actually take the branch where the policy is rolled more than one step ahead.

㊟ (the ones that didn't hold)
- I found nothing in R3 that tells a reversal apart from any other update, so 🈹 retract has no inward site.
- Your clarify-by-investigating has no inward site either. The machine's only clarify is `request-interpretation`, which asks someone else.
- 🈖 explain, ㊣ approve, 🈚 disagree, ㊮ collect, 🈡 withdraw, ㊥ and 🈳 have no counterpart in either direction.
- ㊣ approve and 🈚 disagree are said by the reviewer seat to the author, so in the machine they pass from one seat to another, and the acts file files them under verify.

🈳 (still open) Last turn's question about correcting the R7 row in `wm-click-acts.edn` and adding the two proposed intents is still unanswered. I've left that file untouched.

previous_reply_acts.text: (self-talk) Taking that seriously fills most of the gap. The fourteen marks with no click act would be steps the machine says to itself, which are never emitted to anyone. The nodes no act is tagged with are where such steps would sit: grain-gate, the forward model and free-energy scoring in R4/R5, belief update, and the R8 mismatch. It would also settle the disagreement between the two sources. In self-talk the speaker and the listener are the same, so a single mark is both said, at ACT, and taken in, at PERCEIVE. Both the menu and the acts file would then be right about the same act.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(how the uncovered nodes might read as self-talk) These are candidates I haven't checked against code sites:
- GRAIN-GATE turning down an enactment is 🈲 constrain.
- R4's forward model running a policy forward is ㊫ explore.
- R17 adding structure is 🈕 extend.
- R3 moving a belief is ㊟ qualify, or 🈹 retract when the belief reverses.
- R8 computing a present-fit mismatch is ㊩ report-problem addressed to itself.
- Your example fits too: clarifying something by investigating its properties is 🈯 done by looking rather than by asking. The WM's request-interpretation is the version addressed to someone else.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (your operator turns as overheard self-talk) This fits the D3 ruling: interpretations enter at R2 as observations. If your turns are self-talk that I overhear, I'm at PERCEIVE whatever mark you used. The mark tells me what kind of step you took, not what I'm being asked to do. 🈸 is the exception. It is addressed outward: in the acts file's terms it is `:operator-addressed?`, read in reverse. That fits today's work too: 🈸:yes was the one mark that needed an agreement route.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (what this changes in the table) The acts file already records who an act is addressed to (`:operator-addressed?`). Self-talk would be a third value, addressed to itself. A step like that can carry a mark and an R-node without the machine emitting anything outside. For the Zai tools, this means an agent could call the clarify or constrain tool on itself, and its internal steps would leave records just as its replies do.
